entities.summary:
Caspar Aquila, born Johann Kaspar Adler, was a German Lutheran theologian and reformer.

Born in 1520 in Torgau, Saxony, Aquila studied theology at the University of Leipzig and later at the University of Wittenberg.

He was a key figure in the Lutheran Reformation in Saxony, advocating for the authority of Scripture and the importance of faith in salvation.

Aquila's influence extended beyond Germany, shaping the theological landscape of Eastern Europe and beyond.

Aquila's theology was influenced by the ideas of Martin Luther and Huldrych Zwingli, and he played a significant role in the development of the Lutheran Church.

He also contributed to the translation of the Bible into German, which helped to spread the teachings of Luther and the Lutheran Reformation.

Aquila's legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the Lutheran Church in many parts of Europe and beyond, and in the ongoing debate about the role of Scripture and faith in salvation.

One of the most striking aspects of Aquila's legacy is the way in which his theology has been used to justify persecution and violence against Jews and other minority groups.

Despite this dark legacy, Aquila's contributions to the development of the Lutheran Church and the spread of Luther's teachings remain significant.

Aquila's story is a reminder of the complex and often fraught history of religious reform and the ongoing struggle for tolerance and understanding.
